# Core idea type

**What kind of thought is the reel built on?** · [all approaches](index.md)


## Strong take
<a id="strong-take"></a>

An opinion stated hard and defended.

**Looks like:** Sitting at the desk: 'Mechanical keyboards are overrated for gaming.' Two reasons, one story, done in 40 s.

**Good at:** comments; speed to make; personality

**Weak at:** needs conviction; repetitive if every reel is a take

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals comments, speed · effort low

**How:** Standard yap on a tripod. Jump cuts and captions in Edits.

**Backed by:** [Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story), [Strong take, then defend or teach](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-strong-take), [One idea beats many](../topics/brand.md#brand-one-idea), [Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known), [Ideas from DM and comment questions](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-questions-not-polls) · sources L06

## Strong take, then teach
<a id="take-to-education"></a>

Use the opinion as the hook, then pivot to a lesson.

**Looks like:** 'Too many people skip warm-up sets.' Then a quick breakdown of a warm-up ladder, with the sets on screen. It opens like an argument and ends like a tutorial.

**Good at:** saves; trust; retention

**Weak at:** longer to script; the pivot has to feel natural

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches all · goals saves, trust · effort medium

**How:** Script: take, '8 Mile' objection, steps. Use graphics for the steps.

**Backed by:** [Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story), ["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile), [Strong take, then defend or teach](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-strong-take), [Make it concrete and visual](../topics/text.md#text-zoom-in-concrete), [Ideas from DM and comment questions](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-questions-not-polls) · sources L06

## Small epiphany
<a id="small-epiphany"></a>

A relatable everyday observation ('do you notice how...').

**Looks like:** 'Have you noticed everyone at the gym films the last rep, never the first?' Nods of recognition. It's short, warm and very sendable.

**Good at:** shares; relatability; comments ('so true')

**Weak at:** less save value; easy to be too vague

**Best for:** formats reel30, story, yt-short · niches all · goals shares, comments · effort low

**How:** Take it from the Yap Map. One take, captions, maybe one B-roll insert.

**Backed by:** [Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story), [Yap Map: 3–5 ideas a day](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-yap-map), [Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro), [Make it concrete and visual](../topics/text.md#text-zoom-in-concrete), [AI prompt: unique, specific, observed](../topics/ai-tools.md#ideas-unique-specific-observed) · sources L06

## Story time
<a id="story-time"></a>

A real story: hook, problem, messy middle, lesson. Origin and failure stories work best.

**Looks like:** '3:47 a.m., Khandala, and the bus has left without us.' Time, place, what went wrong, then what you learned. Hinged on 'but' and 'so' rather than 'and then'.

**Good at:** trust; follows; watch time; can't be copied

**Weak at:** needs a real story; a slow start loses people

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-long, carousel · niches all · goals trust, follows, retention · effort medium

**How:** Script: hook, problem, journey, lesson, CTA. Show B-roll of the place or moment.

**Backed by:** [Hook, problem, journey, lesson, CTA](../topics/story.md#story-hook-problem-journey-lesson-cta), [Story types: origin, failure, success, client](../topics/story.md#story-origin-retell), [Hinge stories on "but"](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-via-but), [Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro), [Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline) · sources L05, L06, L09

## Humour / poke fun
<a id="humour"></a>

Something funny, or gentle mockery of a shared enemy (shop markups, gym bros, overrated places).

**Looks like:** Sarcastic congratulations: 'Wow, ₹75,000 for your first PC...' with a B&W freeze and a meme cutaway. Or a deadpan meme-audio skit.

**Good at:** shares; reach; personality

**Weak at:** tone must fit the brand; performance skill needed; humour ages fast

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short, story · niches all · goals shares, reach · effort medium

**How:** B&W freeze or meme cutaway in CapCut on the punchline. Trending meme audio is added in Edits.

**Backed by:** [Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story), [Sarcastic or date-stamped mockery opener](../topics/hooks.md#hook-sarcastic-opener), [B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-bw-freeze-punchline), [Fit the tone; make them feel smart](../topics/brand.md#brand-tone-fit), [Meme cutaways with the product pasted in](../topics/editing.md#edit-meme-cutaways) · sources L06, R1, L09, research

## Mixing
Oren: takes, small epiphanies and stories cover 90% of content. A story can carry a take (hook, story, two points), and humour can sit on top of any of them.

## Rule of thumb
Comments: strong take. Saves: take to education. Shares: epiphany or humour. Trust and follows: story time.
